clue.text: Dog's not in my care? One chained, why not!

indicators.note: chained means linked into the line of words, so the lone letter is fastened in among them

parts.note: a dog called Fido that I am not minding: 'I don't mind Fido'
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to look after a dog, yet happy to tie one up.
explanation.walkthrough: Fido is the stock name for a dog. Chaining I in just before FIDO turns 'I don't mind Fido' into the accepting reply.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a cheerful acceptance of an offer, equivalent in spirit to the exclamation 'why not!'.

clue.text: See 1 across
View work in something charged

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
taken as written
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: Seeing an artwork displayed in something electrified.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a belief or judgement someone holds, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: See 20
One's written about five hundred in accurate digits

indicators.note: the outer pair of letters is written around everything else, enclosing it

parts.note: One is I, and 's gives S

indicators.note: the Roman numeral is set inside the word for accurate

parts.note: nice can mean precise or exact, as in a nice distinction
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A number recorded around 500 among precise figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives I plus S, which surround NDICE (D put inside NICE).
explanation.definitionFit: Index fingers are digits of the hand, so the plural fingers can be called by that name.

clue.text: Range fixed, I love to enter Welsh town going north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means the letters are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: set means fixed or firm

indicators.note: the zero letter goes into the name of the Welsh town

parts.note: Mold is a town in Flintshire, north Wales
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A mountain trip settled on, with a fondness for a Welsh town on the way north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going north' turns the entire built string upwards, not just the town; Mold is a small Flintshire town few non-Welsh solvers know.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dolomites are a mountain range in north-east Italy, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Smothered in ketchup, a Venezuelan flag

indicators.note: the letters are covered over by the surrounding words, buried inside them

explanation.surface: A Venezuelan flag drowned in tomato sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is a verb here: to lay with flagstones.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag a path is to lay it with flagstones, which is to surface it with paving.

clue.text: Arcade game, where Spooner has to throw me away?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words are exchanged

parts.note: to throw away is to bin
the setter of this puzzle is Paul

explanation.surface: A game at the arcades where someone wants to get rid of the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bin Paul' (throw away the setter) with its opening sounds swapped becomes the game; 'away' completes 'throw away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinball is a classic coin-operated machine found in amusement arcades.

clue.text: Loved touring capital city where cyclists race

indicators.note: touring suggests wandering around, so the letters of the first word move about

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Someone enjoyed travelling round a capital with a famous cycle track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' looks like a containment signal wrapping the city, but it is the anagram signal for the first word, whose result simply precedes the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A velodrome is a banked track built for bicycle racing.

clue.text: I'm backed by the party, and — only one brother can win

indicators.note: backed means turned round, so the two letters run in reverse

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician speaks of his party, noting that only one sibling can prevail.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2010 the brothers David and Ed Miliband stood against each other for the British Labour leadership; Ed won.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname identifies the two brothers who contested the 2010 Labour leadership, a contest only one could win.

clue.text: Eternally so desperate to grab husband — might they be?

definitions.text: Eternally so desperate to grab husband — might they be?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take hold of the abbreviation, holding it among them
desperate suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone forever frantic to catch a husband, and asking whether such people are the type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate' rearranges ETERNALLY SO into LONELYEARTS; 'to grab' then puts H in.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonely hearts are people seeking a partner, exactly the kind of person desperate to land a husband.

clue.text: See 12
Soldier, daft Don

parts.note: the punctuation mark in the clue is a comma

indicators.note: daft means crazy, so the letters of the name are jumbled

explanation.surface: A soldier dismissed as a silly fellow named Don.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma itself gives its name as letters; 'daft' turns DON into NDO.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier trained for raids, a specific type of fighter.

clue.text: Finnish, we hear, from these languages?

definitions.text: Finnish, we hear, from these languages?

parts.words: Finnish, we hear, from these languages?
parts.note: Finnish sounds like finish, a wood surface treatment, which here is made from the names of two European tongues

explanation.surface: Asking which languages give rise to Finnish.
explanation.walkthrough: Two languages placed side by side name a high-gloss shellac finish for wooden furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: This lacquering technique is a glossy finish applied to wood, matching the sound of Finnish.

clue.text: Fast kept in check, good to be easing off

indicators.note: the period of fasting is held within the word for restraint

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A fast held under control, which is good for relaxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adjective meaning quick; it is the noun, the fasting season.
explanation.definitionFit: Relenting means softening or yielding, a synonym for easing off.

clue.text: Passport indeed put in storage compartment, as went on leave

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the word for the storage space

parts.note: a hold is the cargo space of a ship or plane
a passport is a form of ID, identification
aye means yes, indeed

explanation.surface: A passport stowed in the luggage hold by someone going away on leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To holiday is to take time off, so having holidayed means having taken leave.

clue.text: Eventually choose home for badger ahead of Trotsky

indicators.note: the badger's home comes before the revolutionary's first name

parts.note: a sett is a badger's burrow
Leon Trotsky was the Russian revolutionary

explanation.surface: A badger's burrow taking precedence over a Russian revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle on something is to decide on it after deliberation, finally choosing.

clue.text: Film review, "Strong hit", nonsense

indicators.note: to review is to look over again, here to rework the letters

parts.note: F is forte, strong or loud in music
to lam is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A critic's write-up of a movie praising a powerful blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' rearranges FILM into FLIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Flimflam is idle talk or humbug, a colourful synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Little child carries gun, like it or loathe it!

indicators.note: carries means the outer word holds the weapon inside itself

parts.note: a mite is a small child
an arm is a weapon such as a gun

explanation.surface: A small child holding a firearm, something people either love or hate.
explanation.walkthrough: Marmite is a British yeast spread famously advertised with the slogan 'love it or hate it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeast spread's own advertising made its divisiveness its signature, so this phrase points to it.

clue.text: No wizards should get face and legs jumbled up

parts.note: mug is slang for face

indicators.note: jumbled up means the letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Ordinary folk who must have their face and legs muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumbled up' turns LEGS into GLES.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Harry Potter books, people without magical powers are called Muggles: non-wizards.

clue.text: Poser, dolly

definitions.meaning: a poser here is someone who poses for an artist or photographer
a dolly is an easy catch in cricket, one that should never be dropped

explanation.walkthrough: 'Poser' suggests a puzzle or a show-off, but it is a model posing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitter is both an artist's model and, in cricket slang, a very easy catch.

clue.text: Alas, the three R's, it's difficult for ill-educated Americans

indicators.note: difficult suggests the letters are awkward, put into a troublesome order

parts.note: three R's are three letters R
the 's is no letter, leaving it

explanation.surface: A lament that reading, writing and arithmetic are hard for poorly schooled Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: The three R's are reading, writing and arithmetic, but here they are just three letter Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: Trailer trash is a derogatory American term for poor, uneducated people living in trailer parks.

clue.text: A derringer initially firing shot beneath someone

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are scrambled
initially takes just the first letter of the gun's name

explanation.surface: A small pistol going off underneath a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges A, D and FIRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra dig, short for Latin infra dignitatem, means below one's dignity, unbecoming for someone.

clue.text: See 9
___ _ Heaven 1: away win welcome

definitions.meaning: a football result is written home team first, so an away victory for Heaven against the underworld reads Hell nil, Heaven one
a greeting given to someone arriving

explanation.walkthrough: Fill the blanks with HELL 0, the zero read as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the standard word of greeting, a synonym of a welcome.

clue.text: Trace element, for example, brought up

parts.note: tin is a chemical element

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means the letters are read upwards, reversed

explanation.surface: A trace element, for instance, coming up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trace element' reads as one phrase, but 'Trace' is the definition and 'element' the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace or hint of something.

clue.text: Island's south as frozen?

parts.note: icily describes acting as if frozen

explanation.surface: Asking whether the southern part of an island is frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily is the large Mediterranean island off the toe of Italy.

clue.text: Hollywood, where Neil Diamond's initials added to triplet of notes

indicators.note: added to means the initials are joined on after the notes

parts.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale, so three notes give la la la

indicators.note: initials means taking the first letter of each name

explanation.surface: The singer Neil Diamond's initials put on a three-note tune in Hollywood.
explanation.definitionFit: La-la land is a jokey nickname for Los Angeles and Hollywood, a place of fantasy.

clue.text: Head of government into Scandinavian money, the beast!

indicators.note: into means the first letter goes inside the currency word

parts.note: the ore is a small coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A government leader dipping into Scandinavian funds, and being a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monstrous creature of folk tales, a kind of beast.

clue.text: Talk sure to be unintelligible at back of night club

indicators.note: at back of puts the scrambled letters after the club

parts.note: a disco is a night club for dancing

indicators.note: unintelligible means garbled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Being sure something will be inaudible at the back of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be unintelligible' rearranges SURE into URSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse means conversation or talk, written or spoken.
